name: Faerie Realm
description: The realm of faeries, in whose stories the player characters often collectively take on the role of the hero.

name: Cailleach
description: A faerie hag that grants sovereignty of Ireland after testing the courage of a man; an example of a giver of final rewards.

name: Ireland
description: Land whose sovereignty the cailleach grants to a man who passes her test of courage.

name: Rumplestiltzkin
description: Fairy-tale figure who provides service and the chance to marry a prince, but becomes a threat; an example of a faerie playing several roles.

name: The Beast
description: The Beast from Beauty and the Beast, initially a threat, then needing help, then giving rewards.

name: The Frog Prince
description: Fairy-tale figure who serves the princess, becomes a moral test, needs to be helped, and grants rewards.

name: The Little Mermaid
description: Fairy-tale heroine who deliberately reverses traditional stories, losing her voice and then her life for love of a mortal.

name: The Bremen Town Musicians
description: Fairy-tale figures cited as examples of faeries who are the heroes of stories.

name: The Gingerbread Man
description: Fairy-tale figure cited as an example of a faerie who is the hero of a story.

name: Cinderella
description: Fairy-tale heroine whose slippers Charles Perrault changed to glass, creating a resonant image.

name: Thirty Six Dramatic Situations
description: Georges Polti's scheme of thirty-six primal emotions driving all dramatic plots, recommended as inspiration for faerie stories (e.g. Supplication, Daring Enterprise, Obtaining).

name: Story Flow
description: Story-planning method dividing a story into thesis, antithesis, and synthesis, fleshed out as six components: hook, trigger, setting, twist, resolution, and consequences.

name: Hook
description: The story component that drags the characters into the action, often connected to a Story or Personality Flaw of a key character.

name: Trigger
description: The precipitating event of a story's plot, dependent on the characters' actions or external to them.

name: Setting
description: Story component describing the location in which most of the action takes place, usually determined by the hook.

name: Twist
description: Story component, especially important in intrigue stories, in which things are not what they first seemed.

name: Resolution
description: The most important part of a story's synthesis: how the situation could be brought to a conclusion, best described as several possible end-states.

name: Consequences
description: Story component covering what results from the characters' actions, including political ramifications and rewards such as experience, Confidence Points, and changes in Personality Traits and Reputations.

name: Token of the Star
description: An example item whose acquisition by the characters could act as a story's trigger.

name: Story Flaw
description: Category of Flaw that can be connected to a story's hook.

name: Personality Flaw
description: Category of Flaw that can be connected to a story's hook, such as a widow appealing to a Compassionate character.

name: Compassionate
description: Personality Flaw cited as an example hook: a widow appeals to the charity of a Compassionate character.

name: Mentor
description: A character's mentor, who may ask the character to perform a small task as a story hook.

name: Personality Traits
description: Character traits that may change as a consequence or reward of a story.

name: Reputation
description: Character reputations that may change as a consequence of a story.

name: Confidence Points
description: Game resource that characters may gain as a reward from a story.

name: Experience Points
description: Game reward characters may gain from completing a story.

name: Dramatic Elements
description: The breakdown of a story's structure into dramatis personae (roles) and acts, following the structure common to folktales.

name: Dramatis Personae
description: The specific roles characters play in fairy tales and myths (hero, villain, donor, helper, princess, task-setter, false hero); one character can combine several roles.

name: Hero
description: Dramatic role of the one who sets off on adventure, either a seeker-hero or a victim-hero; in Faerie stories often taken collectively by the characters.

name: Villain
description: Dramatic role of the one who opposes the hero repeatedly, culminating in a fight, struggle, or pursuit.

name: Donor
description: Dramatic role of one who grants the hero a magical gift or power vital to his task, not necessarily willingly.

name: Helper
description: Dramatic role of one always well-inclined toward the hero, providing timely aid in travel, rescue, or tasks.

name: Princess
description: Dramatic role of the object of the hero's quest or a prize acquired along the way; can be any person or object.

name: Task-Setter
description: Dramatic role that poses challenges for the hero to pass to win the princess, distinct from donor and villain.

name: False Hero
description: Infrequent dramatic role of one who tries to claim credit for the hero's actions, always uncovered in time.

name: Acts
description: Linked scenes in which dramatis personae of a fairy tale interact, such as Interdiction, Villainy, Receipt, Struggle, Ordeal, and Reconciliation.

name: Interdiction
description: Act in which the hero is issued a command by an authority figure which is then violated, sending him on adventure.

name: Reconnaissance
description: Act in which the villain first appears and gathers information about the hero.

name: Trickery
description: Act in which the villain deceives his intended victim to take possession of him or his belongings.

name: Villainy
description: Act in which the villain causes direct harm, or a lack becomes apparent, starting the action of the story.

name: Receipt
description: Act in which the hero gains a magical agent or token from a donor, on which completion of the story always depends.

name: Transference
description: Act in which the hero is transported, delivered, or led to the object of his quest, often by magical means.

name: Struggle
description: Act of direct conflict between hero and villain over the object of the quest, usually ending in the hero's victory.

name: Pursuit
description: Act in which the hero is pursued on his journey home and rescued by magical agent, helper, or quest object.

name: Ordeal
description: Act requiring the hero to perform a difficult task, such as riddles, choice, or tests of strength.

name: Imposture
description: Act in which a false hero claims credit for the hero's deeds before being exposed by an identifying token.

name: Reconciliation
description: Final act of the fairy tale, in which the hero acquires the object he sought, such as a wedding or return home.

name: Odysseus
description: Hero of The Odyssey, cited as an example of the hero role; Hermes showed him the moly plant.

name: Samson
description: Hero of the Book of Judges, cited as an example of the hero role.

name: Es-Sindibad
description: Sinbad, cited as an example of the hero role.

name: Thrym
description: Villain of the Theft of Thor's Hammer, cited as an example of the villain role.

name: Hera
description: Villain in the Sorrows and Labors of Heracles, cited as an example of the villain role.

name: Kostchei the Undying
description: Villain in Maria Morevna, cited as an example of the villain role.

name: Fafnir
description: Figure from the Saga of the Nibelungs cited as an example of a donor.

name: Ceridwen
description: The witch whose cauldron gives Gwion Bach magical powers; example of a donor.

name: Gwion Bach
description: Hero who gains magical powers from Ceridwen's cauldron.

name: Hermes
description: Helper who shows Odysseus the moly plant; example of the helper role.

name: Moly
description: Magical plant shown to Odysseus by Hermes.

name: Grey Wolf
description: Helper in the tale of Prince Ivan; example of the helper role.

name: Sphinx
description: The Sphinx faced by Oedipus, an example of the task-setter role.

name: Oedipus
description: Hero who faced the Sphinx.

name: Golden Fleece
description: Prize guarded by a dragon, cited in an example of the task-setter role.

name: Baba Yaga
description: Figure whom a hero may be forbidden to speak to in a typical interdiction.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The Order, whose members and Houses can be interpreted as 'Kinsmen' in dramatic situations.
